tema: Evaluates whether a 6-month ibudilast regimen improves brain function in patients with ME/CFS.
diseno: Case study (conference abstract) assessing brain function with neuroimaging (fractional anisotropy, according to the keywords); sample size not stated.
hallazgos: No specific results are reported in the available text; the conclusions fragment suggests an improvement in brain function with ibudilast.
conclusion: The authors propose that ibudilast could be a suitable medication to improve brain function in ME/CFS and that studies with cognitive assessment could show effects on brain fog.
triangulacion: Keywords and conclusions are consistent (ibudilast, brain function, brain fog); the 'abstract' is noisy opening text belonging to other abstracts in the same volume (stroke) and provides no information. The evidence is very preliminary.

tema: Compares orthostatic intolerance (OI) in long COVID with that in patients with post-EBV and insidious-onset ME/CFS, to assess whether they are the same disease.
diseno: Case-control study: 14 patients with long COVID, 14 with post-EBV ME/CFS and 14 with insidious-onset ME/CFS; OI history, tilt-table test with extracranial Doppler (cerebral blood flow) and suprasternal Doppler (cardiac index).
hallazgos: There were no differences between the three groups in OI prevalence, heart rate and blood pressure changes, reduction in cerebral blood flow or cardiac index during the tilt test.
conclusion: OI and its objective abnormalities in long COVID are comparable to those of ME/CFS, indicating that it is essentially the same disease triggered by SARS-CoV-2 and should be treated similarly.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions agree on OI, tilt test and post-viral origin; the PDF conclusions go somewhat further by drawing therapeutic implications. The results section of the abstract appears truncated.

tema: Compares neuroimaging abnormalities in multiple sclerosis, major depression and CFS/ME to explore whether they share a common cause.
diseno: Narrative literature review on resting-state functional connectivity, grey and white matter pathology and cerebral perfusion; number of studies not stated.
hallazgos: All three diseases show resting-state connectivity abnormalities, grey and white matter pathology and hypoperfusion, possibly linked to systemic inflammation and regional variations in microglia and astrocytes. Replicated findings indicate that high-resolution SPECT could distinguish CFS from depression.
conclusion: SPECT discriminates CFS from depression, but ionizing radiation and low sensitivity argue against routine use; development of functional MRI techniques, machine learning and multidisciplinary approaches is anticipated.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions (taken from the discussion, with noise from acknowledgements and licence text) agree on connectivity, perfusion and inflammation; the conclusions add a bet on MRI and machine learning over SPECT.

tema: Comprehensive review of ME/CFS covering epidemiology, diagnostic criteria, clinical features, genetic susceptibility and pathophysiology.
diseno: Narrative literature review; no own population.
hallazgos: Describes a disease of unknown aetiology, with onset peaking between 20 and 45 years and a female-to-male ratio of 3:1, diagnosed by exclusion, with a neuro-immune-endocrine pattern as a possible key; mentions mitochondrial dysfunction and an infectious hypothesis, none of which explains all cases.
conclusion: Biomarker studies are still frustrating and more knowledge of psychoneurobiology and natural history is needed to develop effective treatments.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions (taken from the discussion, with noise from contributions and funding) are consistent in their pathophysiological and diagnostic approach; the conclusions add a more pessimistic tone about biomarkers than the abstract.

tema: Evaluates a mixed-methods system (semi-structured qualitative interviews plus VAS scales) for measuring PEM after a CPET in ME/CFS.
diseno: Exploratory mixed-methods study with 10 ME/CFS patients and 9 healthy volunteers; VAS for 7 symptoms and interviews at six time points over 72 h before and after a single CPET; Spearman correlations.
hallazgos: Each patient had a unique PEM experience in onset, severity and trajectory; no healthy participant developed PEM. Interviews detected peaks and trajectories that the VAS missed because of ceiling and floor effects; the VAS-interview correlation for fatigue was good at baseline (r=0.7) and poor at peak PEM (r=0.28), improving when the most bothersome symptom was used.
conclusion: Qualitative interviews better capture the evolution of PEM and improve VAS performance; a mixed quantitative-qualitative approach optimizes its measurement.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on the superiority of the mixed approach. The PDF conclusions add caution by calling for validation in larger samples and extend the application to long COVID, which also appears in the keywords.

tema: Looks for molecular signatures of ME/CFS in blood and immune cells and compares them with other diseases featuring fatigue, to identify possible therapeutic targets.
diseno: Case-control study with RNA-seq of whole blood and FACS-sorted PBMC subpopulations; construction of a probabilistic causal model of gene networks. Sample size not stated.
hallazgos: Immune cell type-specific molecular signatures overlapped with those of other fatiguing diseases, pointing to a common molecular aetiology. The causal model identified master regulator genes that modulate network states associated with ME/CFS.
conclusion: The authors propose these master regulator genes as possible therapeutic targets for ME/CFS.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree (PBMC, transcriptome, causal models, therapeutic target). The conclusions text (discussion) is noise: lists of comparisons, software and medRxiv preprint notices, with no usable conclusions.

tema: Reviews the neuroimaging evidence and the assessment of dysautonomia to support neurological involvement in ME/CFS and to look for diagnostic or monitoring biomarkers.
diseno: Narrative literature review on neuroimaging and autonomic testing (COMPASS-31, heart rate variability, Valsalva manoeuvre, tilt table, autoantibodies).
hallazgos: Neuroimaging shows morphological, connectivity, metabolic and functional abnormalities of low specificity. In a subgroup of patients, abnormalities of HRV, the Valsalva manoeuvre and the tilt table are described, along with autoantibodies against adrenergic, cholinergic and serotonergic receptors; the COMPASS-31 serves as a screening tool for dysautonomia.
conclusion: Neuroimaging contributes little to diagnosis, whereas dysautonomia studies in specialized units are promising; ME/CFS is moving toward being seen as a functional pathology involving mainly, but not only, the autonomic nervous system, and the neurologist has an essential role.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on the neuroimaging-dysautonomia axis; the conclusions are more cautious, stressing that the substrate is unknown and that a consensus study protocol is lacking.

tema: Proposes a systems biology model linking low-dose ionizing radiation exposure to the development of chronic fatigue syndrome and immune dysfunction (CFIDS).
diseno: Theoretical model based on literature integration (Chernobyl and US reports); no own sample.
hallazgos: The model proposes that radiation induces bystander effects (RIBE), generation of UVA and internal biophotons, formation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and subsequent immunological effects, also implicating melanoma and haematopoietic dysregulation.
conclusion: The systemic approach allows therapeutic intervention points to be identified (e.g., melanin and L-ergothioneine, under study by the group) and could be applied to other stressors that raise ROS.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent and centred on radiation, RIBE and ROS; the conclusions extend the model to other triggers and mention treatments under investigation not cited in the abstract.

tema: Puts forward a quantum mechanics perspective to explain CFS and its neurological symptoms.
diseno: Theoretical/speculative essay; no population or empirical methods stated.
hallazgos: The opening text describes CFS (prolonged fatigue, unrefreshing sleep, post-exertional malaise, orthostatic intolerance, brain fog) and its social impact; the conclusions discuss possible subtle neurological effects of radiofrequency in susceptible people and the use of music therapy or transcranial magnetic stimulation.
conclusion: Suggests investigating modifications to radiofrequency communications, electromagnetically quiet spaces and complementary therapies, without an alarmist tone.
triangulacion: The keywords (quantum consciousness, PEM, orthostatic intolerance) and the abstract describe the disease, but the conclusions (from the discussion) drift toward radiofrequency and environmental pollution, a focus not announced in the abstract; coherence is partial.

tema: Characterizes the dynamics of cortisol secretion in fibromyalgia with and without CFS compared with healthy controls using a systems theory approach.
diseno: Case-control study with cortisol data from a previous controlled study; two-step coordinate-descent deconvolution (sparse recovery and estimation of infusion and clearance rates). Sample size not stated.
hallazgos: The hepatic cortisol clearance rate was relatively lower in patients, with greater serum accumulation and a delayed cortisol decline response.
conclusion: The results are preliminary; the cortisol change may be adaptive and does not by itself imply a pathological mechanism, so further verification and inclusion of ACTH data are required.
triangulacion: Abstract and conclusions agree on the lower cortisol clearance; the conclusions are more cautious (limited data, possible counter-regulatory mechanism). The keywords reflect the methodological focus well.

tema: Review of gastrointestinal and irritable bowel symptoms in ME/CFS and of the evidence on probiotics as treatment.
diseno: Systematic review in PubMed, Scopus, Medline and EMBASE; 3381 records, 25 studies included (24 RCTs), with quality assessment.
hallazgos: The evidence on probiotics in IBS was of excellent quality, but the evidence in ME/CFS was scarce and of low quality.
conclusion: There is insufficient evidence to recommend probiotics in ME/CFS for GI symptoms; standardized protocols and more research are needed.
triangulacion: The three sources agree; the conclusions explicitly add that active prescription is not recommended and mention the microbiota as a possible factor not addressed.

tema: Editorial introducing a multidisciplinary special issue of Clinical Therapeutics on the diagnosis, pathogenesis and treatment of ME/CFS.
diseno: Editorial; no population or methods stated.
hallazgos: Notes that studies on viral aetiology, mitochondrial dysfunction and cytokines have been inconclusive with adequate sedentary controls, and summarizes articles on oxidative stress, the autonomic nervous system, endocrine-immune regulation, epigenetics, autoantibodies and antibodies against EBV dUTPase.
conclusion: We are still far from understanding and treating the disease; future studies should focus on immunoregulatory molecules, especially in the diencephalon.
triangulacion: The abstract is the opening text of the editorial and the conclusions come from its final part; both are consistent. The keywords (fatigue, homeostasis) are generic and reflect the temperature dysregulation mentioned.

tema: Proposes a unifying concept of ME/CFS pathophysiology based on the finding of autoantibodies against the β2-adrenergic receptor and the M3 muscarinic receptor.
diseno: Theoretical article integrating the authors' own findings (elevated autoantibodies in a subgroup of patients) with the literature on vascular dysfunction, hypoperfusion and metabolism.
hallazgos: Elevated autoantibodies against β2AdR and M3 are described in a subgroup of patients; since both receptors are vasodilators, their dysfunction would produce vasoconstriction and hypoxaemia, in line with the muscle and cerebral hypoperfusion and the metabolic changes described in ME/CFS.
conclusion: β2AdR dysfunction (due to autoantibodies, polymorphisms or desensitization by high sympathetic tone) would be a key factor; the excess of algesic vasodilators generated in muscle could explain hypovolaemia, preload failure and symptoms such as pain, hyperalgesia and flu-like symptoms.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent (autoantibodies, hypoxia, hypoperfusion, autonomic dysfunction); the conclusions extend the model toward functional sympatholysis and algesic vasodilators, not anticipated in the keywords.

tema: Thesis investigating the mechanisms of TORC1, AMPK and mitochondrial complex V in ME/CFS using the Dictyostelium discoideum model.
diseno: Experimental study in the model organism D. discoideum through genetic manipulation (TORC1/AMPK activation, ATP12 expression) and measurements of mitochondrial respiration. No human population.
hallazgos: TORC1 activation increased respiratory activity and ATP without reducing respiratory function; AMPK activation did not alter respiration but inhibited TORC1; the induced complex V defect raised respiration differently from TORC1/AMPK.
conclusion: The higher TORC1 activity in ME/CFS cells could explain the compensatory regulation of respiration, but probably not the isolated inefficiency of complex V, which may occur independently.
triangulacion: There are no keywords and the abstract is only an index, so the only informative source is the conclusions (from the discussion); triangulation is not possible.

tema: Objectively compares the sleep of CFS patients and healthy controls using polysomnography over three consecutive nights.
diseno: Case-control study with 22 CFS patients (CDC 1994 criteria) and 22 healthy controls; three-night polysomnography, analysing the third night, and self-reported insomnia measures.
hallazgos: 9.1% of patients met criteria for an objectively identifiable sleep disorder. There were differences in four objective variables (wake after sleep onset, sleep efficiency, percentage of wakefulness and REM latency) and patients reported more severe insomnia.
conclusion: CFS patients sleep worse by objective and subjective measures; a detailed sleep history is advisable to rule out sleep disorders, and improving sleep is a possible therapeutic target.
triangulacion: The three sources are fully consistent; the conclusions come from the structured abstract and match it word for word. The keywords reflect the polysomnographic variables highlighted.

tema: Compares the efficacy of valacyclovir, valganciclovir and artesunate in reactivated HHV-6 and HHV-7 infections associated with ME/CFS.
diseno: Non-randomized controlled comparative study: 255 patients with HHV-6/HHV-7 reactivation confirmed by PCR in leukocytes; 192 treated for 3 months with valacyclovir (3000 mg/day), valganciclovir (900 mg/day) or artesunate (100 mg/day) and 63 controls without antivirals.
hallazgos: PCR negativization at month three was 37% and 34% (HHV-6/HHV-7) with valacyclovir, 48% and 45% with valganciclovir and 68% and 63% with artesunate (P < 0.05).
conclusion: Artesunate was the most effective, valganciclovir moderate and valacyclovir the least effective; many patients resisted all regimens, so higher doses, longer or combined treatments and double-blind randomized trials are needed.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on the superiority of artesunate; the conclusions are more cautious in pointing out the resistance of many patients and the need for controlled trials.

tema: Looks for a gene expression signature that would allow biomarkers of post-infectious ME/CFS to be identified.
diseno: Case-control study with whole-genome Affymetrix microarrays (about 39,000 transcripts) in PBMC from men with post-infectious chronic fatigue (n = 8) and healthy male controls (n = 7).
hallazgos: Patients and controls differed in the expression of 366 genes, related to immunomodulation, oxidative stress and apoptosis. Prototype biomarkers were identified, with some overlap with previous microarrays.
conclusion: The authors see these genes as a first step toward diagnostic biomarkers and an explanation of the mechanism of post-infectious fatigue, although they clarify that ME/CFS would not be primarily genetic.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on differential expression, immunomodulation and oxidative stress. The PDF conclusions are more cautious than the abstract: they point out the poor concordance between microarray studies, that mRNA is only a snapshot in time and the need to validate with RT-PCR, western blot and ELISA, without being able to distinguish cause from effect.

tema: To build a map of metabolic phenotypes (metabotypes) in the serum of ME/CFS patients.
diseno: Case-control study: 83 patients and 35 healthy controls; global metabolomics, lipidomics and hormone measurement with exploratory analysis.
hallazgos: Common changes compatible with high energy strain and altered use of fatty acids and amino acids as fuel; in addition, three subgroups with heterogeneous effects, two with energy dysregulation, supported by clinical data.
conclusion: They propose that the energy strain could derive from tissue hypoxia triggered by exertion and that metabolic dysfunction is a likely mediator of symptoms and a possible therapeutic target.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent (metabolomics, lipidomics, hormones, energy metabolism); no conclusions are available for comparison.

tema: Meta-ethnography on the support needs of people with CFS/ME from a relational approach to invisible illness.
diseno: Meta-ethnography (systematic synthesis of qualitative studies) on users' experiences; number of included studies not stated in the available text.
hallazgos: The experience of CFS/ME is shaped by relationships (e.g., the risk of the clinical consultation); patients and professionals may feel unheard and patients are constructed as blameworthy; there are successful collaborations in symptom management.
conclusion: A relational paradigm shift is needed that moves away from individual blame and promotes the co-creation of useful 'relational goods' between patients and professionals, with dissemination of the framework in primary care.
triangulacion: Keywords (invisible illness, relational goods, social networks) and conclusions converge on the relational approach; the abstract is opening text (the article's header and keywords) and only confirms the meta-ethnographic design.

tema: Proposes a neuroinflammatory model that explains the onset, symptoms and flare-ups of ME/CFS.
diseno: Theoretical opinion article (viewpoint); no own population.
hallazgos: Triggers such as severe viral infections, toxins or emotional trauma would disturb the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus and induce glia-mediated neuroinflammation; limbic, hypothalamic and autonomic dysfunction would explain the symptoms, and stressors exceeding a threshold provoke relapses that perpetuate the disease.
conclusion: If it is shown to be neuroinflammatory, ME/CFS would be potentially reversible; mentions drugs that attenuate glia (low-dose naltrexone, CT38) and possible biomarkers.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions (from the discussion) are consistent on the hypothalamus-neuroinflammation axis; the conclusions add a hopeful tone and references to treatments not present in the abstract.

tema: Evaluates single-cell Raman microspectroscopy to find biomarkers of mitochondrial dysfunction in ME/CFS.
diseno: Experimental study with ρ0 cells (lacking mitochondrial DNA) as a model and PBMC from ME/CFS patients (n = 80) and healthy controls (n = 126); single-cell Raman spectra with machine learning classification and mitochondrial stress tests.
hallazgos: Phenylalanine Raman bands were elevated in ρ0 cells and in patient PBMC compared with their controls. The classification model reached an accuracy of 98.1% (sensitivity of 96.3% in patients and 99.2% in controls).
conclusion: Intracellular phenylalanine could be a biomarker linked to mitochondrial and energy dysfunction, and Raman combined with machine learning could serve as a diagnostic tool.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions agree fully (phenylalanine, mitochondrial dysfunction, ρ0 cells, PBMC). The conclusions only add the detailed sensitivity figures and the sample size.

tema: Refines a model linking CFS to idiopathic intracranial hypertension by incorporating CSF leak, with obstruction of cranial venous drainage as the primary structural cause.
diseno: Theoretical article; includes no own empirical data.
hallazgos: According to the model, cranial venous obstruction (subtle, intermittent or mistaken for normal anatomy) raises intracranial pressure, stresses the dura and can cause CSF leak, generating a spectrum that includes idiopathic intracranial hypertension, CFS, fibromyalgia and spontaneous intracranial hypotension.
conclusion: In CFS a normal intracranial pressure does not exclude a significant physiological abnormality; the authors suggest that a similar mechanism could operate in other medically unexplained syndromes.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent; the PDF conclusions develop the clinical spectrum and speculatively extend the mechanism to other unexplained syndromes.

tema: Pilot study analysing the immune cell proteome in long COVID and comparing it with that of ME/CFS to see whether they share pathophysiology.
diseno: Quantitative PBMC proteomics in long COVID patients (n = 6) and controls (n = 5), compared with a previous ME/CFS dataset (n = 9) analysed with the same methodology; PCA and Markov clustering analysis.
hallazgos: 3131 proteins were analysed: 162 were differentially regulated (37 immune and 21 mitochondrial), and PCA separated all patients from controls. There were clusters and pathways overlapping with ME/CFS, mainly in immune functions and mitochondrial energy production.
conclusion: Both diseases appear to share an immune and mitochondrial pathophysiology. The authors attribute it to an inappropriate immune response that becomes chronic in susceptible individuals.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on the immune and mitochondrial overlap between long COVID and ME/CFS. The conclusions acknowledge the small sample size, defend the validity of small cohorts and add the heterogeneity of long COVID (four clinical phenotypes), a nuance absent from the abstract.

tema: Analyses the monocyte transcriptome in post-Q fever fatigue syndrome (QFS) and in ME/CFS, focusing on the mitochondria-derived peptides humanin and MOTS-c.
diseno: Case-control study matched for age and sex: QFS (n = 10), ME/CFS (n = 10), asymptomatic Q fever seropositive individuals (n = 10) and healthy controls (n = 10); monocyte RNA-seq and humanin measurement.
hallazgos: The genes MT-RNR2 (humanin) and MT-RNR1 (MOTS-c) showed decreased expression in QFS, ME/CFS and, to a lesser degree, in asymptomatic seropositive individuals compared with healthy controls. Circulating humanin was lower (median 364 pg/mL in ME/CFS).
conclusion: These peptides could be important in the pathophysiology of QFS and ME/CFS, although their role remains unclear and merits further study.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions agree on humanin, MOTS-c and the QFS/ME/CFS comparison. The conclusions are more cautious than the abstract: since the decrease also appears in asymptomatic seropositive individuals, the finding might not be specific to chronic fatigue.

tema: Describes the clinical profile of British patients with POTS and their experience with the health system.
diseno: Survey developed by professionals, patients and the association PoTS UK; 779 responses from UK patients with POTS were analysed.
hallazgos: The most frequent initial triad was fatigue, dizziness and palpitations; the mean diagnostic delay was almost four years and erroneous psychiatric labelling was common. 23% used a wheelchair and 37% could not work; only a quarter received advice to exercise.
conclusion: Training health professionals is recommended to avoid misdiagnosis and improve services, especially accessible rehabilitation.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on diagnostic delay, psychiatric misdiagnosis and the impact on quality of life; the discussion adds the focus on exercise rehabilitation and on patients' research priorities (lifestyle changes), absent from the keywords.
